paper_title: ThermoDSE: A Thermal-Aware and Comprehensive Design Space Exploration for Chiplet-Based DNN Accelerators

scenario.figure_or_table: Table IV (row 'Ours'); thermal map in Fig. 10(b) on PDF page 12
scenario.description: ThermoDSE-optimized design under a 300 mm2 interposer area and 75 C peak-temperature constraint: 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm inter-chiplet spacing, 240 GB/s NoC/NoP bandwidth, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array. Reported results are peak temperature 74.8 C, energy 59.8 mJ, delay 2.01 ms, yield 0.911, EDYP cost 132.2. The paper publishes no per-block coordinates, dimensions or power values for this design.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D chiplet-based DNN accelerator (Arch-S, fine-grained task orchestration), with compute dies and an I/O die on a passive interposer, TIM, heat spreader and heat sink
scenario.workload: AR/VR multi-DNN mix of ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net and BERT-Small (Table III)
scenario.operating_point: 1.8 GHz, 14 nm scaled, 4-channel DRAM at 128 GB/s; HotSpot 6.0 steady-state with 45 C ambient and 0.4 K/W convection resistance; peak temperature 74.8 C

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal simulation, fed with component-wise average power, a floorplan and material properties (PDF pages 4 and 7). Ambient is 45 C with 0.4 K/W convection resistance (PDF page 9). TIM, heat spreader and heat sink properties are taken from TESA [12]. NoP power is assumed spatially distributed across the interposer. Performance, energy, area and yield come from an in-house analytical and fine-grained simulator.
original_setup.optimizer: ThermoDSE: TED (transductive experimental design) initialization followed by SCBO (scalable constrained Bayesian optimization) with GP surrogates, implemented in BoTorch. Trust-region threshold th=16 is used for the SA/RL comparison (PDF pages 7-9, 12). The optimizer baselines are SA (from TESA) and PPO-based RL (from Chiplet-Gym).
original_setup.controller: No runtime thermal controller. DVFS is discussed and rejected as unsuitable for sequential multi-DNN edge workloads (PDF page 3). Thermal management is design-time only: greedy thermal-aware task mapping that places the highest-power microtasks on corner cores and lower-power ones on center cores, plus inter-chiplet spacing (ICS) selection (PDF page 5).
original_setup.benchmark: AR/VR multi-DNN workload of ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net and BERT-Small (Table III, PDF page 9). Selected scenario is the 'Ours' row of Table IV (PDF page 10): 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 240 GB/s NoC bandwidth, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array. Constraints are 300 mm2 interposer area and 75 C peak temperature. Baselines are Simba-like (B1), TESA (B2), TESA* (B3) and Chiplet-Gym (B4).

thermal_observable.location: Peak temperature of the optimized ThermoDSE design, as reported in the Table IV 'Ours' row. The spatial thermal map is shown in Fig. 10(b) on PDF page 12 but not quantified per block.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (peak) temperature across the chip from the HotSpot 6.0 steady-state simulation, using average power over the AR/VR multi-DNN workload

physical_mismatches.reason: The packet has no pinned assets or paper-linked resources (artifact search found no links; assets list empty). No per-block coordinates, dimensions or power values are published for the selected design, so no complete floorplan or power input exists.

The paper models a 2.5D system with an interposer, BEOL layers, micro-bumps, a TIM/heat spreader/heat sink stack and distributed NoP power. A simple 2D steady-state Studio model cannot reproduce this stack or the interposer-level D2D heat coupling. Compute dies and an I/O die are separate, with ICS-dependent lateral coupling.

The paper's thermal result comes from workload-averaged component power from its own energy/latency simulator, with fine-grained task mapping. A one-row illustrative power trace has no equivalent of this, so the paper's workload-derived power distribution cannot be reproduced.
The optimizer (TED+SCBO) and design-space search are outside a thermal-solver runner. Only a single design point could be evaluated, not the DSE result.

No transient behavior, runtime controller or DVFS is modeled in the paper, which is steady-state only. Reliability and yield are modeled analytically, not thermally. This is a mismatch only if the Studio assumes transient dynamics.

3D stacking is explicitly out of scope (future work, PDF page 13). The cooling model is a fixed 0.4 K/W convection resistance with 45 C ambient and TESA-derived materials, which may differ from Studio defaults.

studio_assumptions: Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative 2D placement, not a replication of the paper's HotSpot 6.0 result.
Generated coordinates would be kept distinct from paper-derived facts, and any one-row power trace would be an assumption.

Studio package/material assumptions (die, interposer, TIM, spreader, heat sink properties and boundary conditions) are not extracted here. The paper does not publish its HotSpot material values, which are cited from TESA [12].
Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 74.8 C.
missing_inputs: Per-block floorplan coordinates x_m, y_m and dimensions width_m, height_m for the 5x4 core, 1x2 chiplet design. Only an area breakdown (Fig. 10(a)) and a thermal map (Fig. 10(b)) are given graphically, not as numeric geometry.
Per-block power values (watts) for the selected design. Only energy (59.8 mJ) and delay (2.01 ms) are given, and total power must not be split without a published rule.
HotSpot configuration files, material property values and layer thicknesses (TIM, heat spreader, heat sink, interposer).
Code, repository, configuration or supplementary data. No availability statement or URL is present in the paper packet, and no pinned assets were supplied.
Final placement, I/O die size and power time series. The workload power is only an averaged quantity and is not published.
Exact die and interposer dimensions. The 300 mm2 interposer area is a constraint, not a published geometry.
